evidence: ibm01 1.0381->0.7819 in 60s of exact-gated local search, zero overlaps; leaderboard rank-1 average is 0.9507
mechanism: The official TILOS proxy evaluator is pure Python at ~0.6 evals/s. Reimplementing it EXACTLY as a GPU-batched tensor program gives ~12000 evals/s (20000x) on ibm01, verified to 1e-15 against the untouched evaluator on 4 structurally different placements per circuit. The two enabling reductions: routing demand is a union of axis-aligned segments, so each route becomes an O(1) write into a difference array plus one cumsum instead of a per-cell loop; macro blockage and density are separable in x and y, so each is a single [R,M]@[M,C] matmul. With that, every accepted move can be gated on the TRUE objective instead of a surrogate -- which is exactly the gap every competing placer pays for.

evidence: ibm01: 5993 driver-keyed nets vs net_cnt 7269; driver weights histogram {1:5309, 2:364, 3:170, 4:81, ...}
mechanism: The challenge ships preprocessed .pt benchmarks whose loader hardcodes net_weights=1.0 and reports num_nets=len(driver-keyed nets). The official wirelength weights every net by its DRIVER PIN weight (up to 10x on ibm01) and normalizes by plc.net_cnt (7269), not by that length (5993). Building an engine on the convenience format would have produced a plausible-but-wrong objective that no amount of search could reconcile. Extract from the authoritative object, never from the convenience export.

evidence: ibm01 initial placement (grid-aligned): CUDA congestion 1.13623884 vs reference 1.13615174; 3 random placements matched to 1e-15 and hid the bug
mechanism: PyTorch folds tensor/python-float into multiply-by-reciprocal on CUDA, which is NOT correctly rounded: 9.69/0.51 returns 18.999999999999996 instead of 19.0. When the quotient feeds a floor() that decides grid-cell membership -- a hard branch in the objective -- that single ULP moves a pin into the neighbouring cell and changes the score. CPU matched the reference and CUDA did not, on the SAME code. Fix: divide by a 0-dim tensor, which forces true IEEE division. Generalizes: any exact port of a quantized/binned objective must use tensor divisors, and must be validated on grid-ALIGNED inputs, which are precisely the ones that expose it.

evidence: 3-circuit dev A/B at 45s: base 0.98248; +cold-row/col 0.99523; +aniso 1.5 0.99042; both 0.99930. Hit rates ibm17: toward 22.2%, axis 11.9%, gauss 11.9%, away 8.3%, coldrow 3.5%, coldcol 2.6%, jump 1.3%
mechanism: Derived a correct structural fact (the congestion model is anisotropic and row/column STRIPED: H demand is laid along the driver's row, V along the sink's column, and horizontal capacity is 1.08-1.87x scarcer on every circuit) and built the operators it implies -- relocate to a cold row / cold column, bias displacements vertically. All three LOST. In a batched search with an exact accept gate, every operator competes for the same scarce resource, a slot in the batch, and a slot spent on a 3%-hit-rate operator is a slot not spent on a 22%-hit-rate one. The figure of merit is measured improving-hit-rate per slot, not mechanistic plausibility. Corollary: measure per-operator yield FIRST, then let a bandit allocate slots, rather than hand-designing the mixture from theory.

evidence: 3 dev circuits at 45s: fixed 0.98582; adaptive alpha=0.15 0.99356; adaptive alpha=0.30 0.99136; toward-heavy fixed 1.01173
mechanism: Bandit/probability-matching over move operators, credited by exactly-measured gain per batch slot, LOSES to a fixed near-uniform mixture (0.98582 -> 0.99356), and hand-boosting the single highest-yield operator loses 3x more (+0.0259). The high-hit-rate operator was the connectivity pull 'toward' (22% vs 1.3% for random jumps): it is easy to improve on early and then self-extinguishes, and it drags the layout into the wirelength-collapsed basin that costs density and congestion. Greedy credit assignment converts the low-yield isotropic operators -- which are buying exploration, not immediate gain -- into slots for an operator with no runway left. Probability matching presumes a stationary reward; operator yield in an exact-gated local search is non-stationary AND self-extinguishing, so measured short-term yield is an actively misleading allocation signal. REFUTES the common claim that adaptive operator selection beats fixed schedules.

evidence: 3 dev circuits, 90s: BPX-only 0.97133, analytical-only 0.97907, analytical->BPX 0.92567. Relaxation tracks the exact congestion to within 7% on ibm17 (2.60 vs 2.43).
mechanism: When an objective is piecewise CONSTANT because it bins continuous positions into cells, do not hand-design a smooth surrogate -- dequantize the objective itself. Replace only the binning: a pin splits bilinearly between adjacent cells instead of snapping to floor(x/gw), and a route occupies the CONTINUOUS interval between its endpoints instead of an integer column range. Every other term (top-k means, capacity normalization, smoothing, blockage) is already differentiable and is carried over verbatim. Both replacements conserve total mass, so the relaxation is unbiased -- it spreads demand smoothly without systematically over- or under-counting. Result: one backward pass gives a gradient for ALL macros where the true gradient is zero almost everywhere, and because an exact engine still decides what is ACCEPTED, a mis-modelled term costs time but can never corrupt the score. Beats both pure discrete search and pure analytical descent.

evidence: 90s/3 dev circuits: 1 cycle 0.92716, 2 cycles 0.93512, 3 cycles 0.93588; 3 basins 0.93634, 5 basins 0.93826 vs 0.92747 single. 300s/2 circuits: 1 cycle 0.97772 vs 3 cycles 0.97994.
mechanism: Three separate breadth mechanisms -- multi-cycle alternation, basin selection by successive halving over diversified probes, and restarts -- ALL lost to a single deep run, and lost by less as the budget grew (cycles: +0.0087 at 90s, +0.0022 at 300s). The common cause is that the global stage has a CONVERGENCE TIME (~30s here): any breadth scheme that allocates less than that per probe is ranking noise while spending budget taken from the stage that was paying. The rule that transfers: measure the convergence time of the component that chooses the basin, and only buy breadth in units larger than it. Below that threshold, depth strictly dominates -- which inverts the usual multi-start advice.

evidence: archgen-ai/Macro-Placement-challenge-2026 submissions/final_placer.py: EVO_CONGESTION_WEIGHT=2.5, EVO_DENSITY_WEIGHT=1.0, EVO_WL_WEIGHT=1.0, PAD80_CD_TIME=3180, PAD80_PCTL=80
mechanism: The challenge required winning entries to open-source under Apache/GPL, so the rank-1, rank-2 and innovation-award implementations are all public. Reading them yielded two things no amount of local search would have: (1) INDEPENDENT CONFIRMATION of our own measured finding -- the rank-1 entry optimizes WL:density:congestion = 1:1:2.5 internally against an official 1:0.5:0.5, exactly the congestion-heavy internal weighting our weight-schedule experiment found; and (2) a structural rule we had not tested -- pad the smaller 80% of macros outward while anchoring the largest 20%, which works because density and congestion are TOP-k statistics so only a few over-full cells cost anything, and small macros are what can move into the gaps without dragging the blocks that anchor the nets. Also calibrated the runtime frontier: their config runs 3180-3420 s/circuit, so a method at 300 s is competing at 1/10th the budget.

evidence: 3 dev circuits at 90s: full-recompute B=512 0.92623 -> incremental B=2048 0.90101 (-0.025). ibm17 1.2148 -> 1.1688, better than the rank-1 entry's worst circuit (1.1839) which they produced at 3180s/circuit.
mechanism: A batched evaluator scores B candidates from scratch, but in a local search every candidate differs from the incumbent in ONE variable, so nearly all of that work is recomputation of unchanged structure. Cache the incumbent's DIFFERENCE arrays and, per candidate, retract the affected nets' routes at the old position and re-emit them at the new one. On ibm17 the affected pins are ~104 of 133,186 (median), so the dominant segmented sort shrinks by ~130x and the per-candidate cost falls to O(affected_pins + grid_cells). This is EXACT, not approximate -- max error 2.2e-16 against the full engine -- so the accept gate keeps its guarantee. 52x throughput on the largest circuit, and the gain is biggest exactly where the method was weakest. GENERAL RULE: before buying more search time, check whether the evaluator is recomputing things the move did not touch; a 50x exact speedup beat every algorithmic variation tried (all of which were within +-0.002 noise).

evidence: ariane133 NG45, ORFS 26Q3-1425-g5da4a78ec6, clock period 4.0ns: ours WNS 0.504007 TNS 0 hold 0.0118443 WL 4608330um area 4306330um2 power 0.199253W Fmax 286.04; reference WNS 0.384924 TNS 0 hold 0.0207239 WL 4574508um area 4306330um2 power 0.19841W Fmax 276.62
mechanism: The challenge organizers' own closing note warns that optimizing the proxy alone is not sufficient for production-ready placements, so we tested it: the SAME OpenROAD flow (synthesis through detailed routing) was run on the design's reference macro placement and on ours, on ariane133 NG45, changing nothing but the macro coordinates. A 12.6% proxy improvement (0.7109 -> 0.6214) produced WNS 0.3849 -> 0.5040 ns (+31%) and Fmax 276.6 -> 286.0 MHz (+3.4%) at IDENTICAL area, with TNS zero in both and hold met in both, for 0.7% more routed wirelength. So on this design the proxy is a faithful surrogate for timing. Note the direction of the wirelength term: our optimizer deliberately INCREASES proxy wirelength (it is only 4% of the objective) and routed wirelength still barely moves -- the gain comes from congestion, not from wire.

evidence: ariane136: proxy 0.7097 -> 0.6223 optimized, ORFS aborts PDN-0179; with 14um clearance push proxy 0.6938 and the flow proceeds. ariane133 at the same settings completed without any clearance push.
mechanism: The Tier-1 proxy contains no clearance term, so an optimizer that gates on the exact proxy packs hard macros until they nearly touch -- that is optimal for the metric and unbuildable in practice. On ariane136 the OpenROAD flow ABORTED at power-grid insertion (PDN-0179 'unable to repair all channels', a 25.7 um residual channel); the same method on ariane133 happened to leave wide enough channels and completed. The failure is design-dependent, so a single successful Tier-2 design does not prove the placements are routable. Fix: push hard macros to a minimum gap (>=12-14 um; the challenge's own rules recommend >=12 um for PDN) as a Tier-2 EXPORT step only. It costs proxy -- 0.6244 -> 0.6938 on ariane136, ~11% -- which is precisely the measure of how much of the proxy optimum was bought with unbuildable tightness. GENERAL RULE: when a benchmark metric omits a manufacturability constraint, an exact-metric optimizer will spend the whole omission, and the omission has to be re-imposed explicitly.

evidence: ariane136: raw export aborts PDN; 14um and 25um uniform clearance both still abort (25um is geometrically impossible, min gap -12um); core-fill x1.25 completes the full flow with WNS 0.1765 vs reference 0.1455 (+21.3%), Fmax 261.54 vs 259.44, identical area, TNS 0 both.
mechanism: Our Tier-2 placement aborted OpenROAD's power grid (PDN-0179) while the design's own reference routed fine, and the obvious explanations were all WRONG when measured: our macro-to-macro gaps were LARGER than the reference (min 14.0 vs 10.0 um), and the evaluator's own 12 um spacing enforcement had already run on both. Extracting the actual ORFS-frame coordinates showed the real difference: the reference SPANS MORE AREA. The Tier-1 proxy canvas (1446 um) is smaller than the ORFS core (2052x2100), the export centres one inside the other, and a placement that respects the canvas therefore leaves ~300 um of unused margin on every side and crams all its routing channels into the middle -- 5th-percentile horizontal channel 12.0 um for us versus 27.0 um for the reference, which is not even canvas-legal (18 of its hard macros extend past the canvas). Expanding our layout about its centre by 1.25x for the Tier-2 export reproduces the reference's channel statistics (H-channel p5 25.5 um) and the flow completes. GENERAL RULE: the optimizer's canvas and the manufacturable core are different objects; optimize in one and EXPORT into the other. Costs nothing here because Tier-1 ranks IBM circuits and Tier-2 uses NG45 designs.

Attempted to reproduce the challenge's published RePlAce baseline ourselves rather than only citing it: converted an ICCAD04 benchmark to LEF/DEF (using the rank-1 entry's published converter) and ran OpenROAD's global_placement, which IS RePlAce. Result on ibm01: 1.5515 legalized, against a published 0.9976 -- 55% worse. Sweeping the target density across 0.55/0.70/0.85/0.95 moves it only between 1.5536 and 1.5669, so the gap is STRUCTURAL, not a tuning miss: the synthetic LEF/DEF has invented routing layers and pitches, and the published baseline comes from the TILOS flow's full mixed-size placement with real technology data plus a macro-placement stage we do not replicate. CONCLUSION: report the published RePlAce number as REPORTED and do not claim a reproduction. Presenting our 1.5515 as 'RePlAce' would have flattered our method by 0.6 proxy against a baseline that is simply broken -- the same straw-man failure mode already caught once in this campaign with an untuned SA temperature.

evidence: ariane136: RTL-MP mapped into the proxy frame scores 1.1782 with legality FALSE (out-of-bounds after clamping); reference 0.7097; ours 0.6223. All 136 macros mapped correctly (25/25 groups).
mechanism: Ran OpenROAD's own RTL-MP macro placer to get a real competitor LAYOUT rather than a copied number, then scored it with our exact Tier-1 evaluator: 1.1782 versus our 0.6223. That comparison is INVALID and was discarded. RTL-MP optimizes its own objective over the real 2052x2100 ORFS core; the Tier-1 proxy canvas is 1446 um, so converting its coordinates into the proxy frame pushes macros out of bounds (the legality check fails) and the clamping alone degrades the score. A placer must be compared on the objective and in the frame it was built for -- RTL-MP is a legitimate Tier-2 competitor (compare WNS/TNS/area through the same ORFS flow) and not a Tier-1 one. Reporting the 1.1782 would have manufactured a 0.56-proxy win over a tool that was never playing our game.

evidence: ariane133 through identical ORFS flow: reference WNS 0.384924 Fmax 276.62; ours no-fill WNS 0.504007 Fmax 286.04; ours core-fill x1.25 WNS 0.553000 Fmax 290.10, WL 4672157 vs 4574508 ref, area identical 4306330, TNS 0 in all three.
mechanism: Core-fill was introduced to FIX a power-grid failure on ariane136, so the obvious read is that it is a routability workaround that costs quality. Testing it on ariane133 -- where the flow already completed without it -- shows the opposite: WNS 0.5040 -> 0.5530 (+9.7% further) and Fmax 286.04 -> 290.10, TNS still zero, area identical. Expanding into the real core is therefore a genuine placement improvement, not a concession: the extra room buys routing channels that shorten critical paths, and the Tier-1 proxy cannot see any of it because its canvas is smaller than the core the chip is actually built in. Against the reference this compounds to WNS +43.7% on ariane133.

evidence: 3 dev circuits at 400s: benchmark init 0.89957 (ibm01 0.7656 ibm09 0.7565 ibm17 1.1766); random init 1.60969 (1.3701 / 1.1723 / 2.2867).
mechanism: The KB carried a WIN for cold-seeded-sa on no_5_on_sphere: warm-seeding from a reference TRAPPED that search because a reference set there is MAXIMAL, so every move is downhill. That reasoning does not transfer here and we tested rather than assumed. Starting from a uniform-random placement instead of the benchmark's hand-crafted one gives 1.60969 versus 0.89957 at an identical 400s budget on three dev circuits -- 79% worse. Mechanism: the ICCAD04 initial placements are not maximal objects, they are hand-crafted layouts that already encode which modules belong near each other, and that information is worth far more than the basin diversity a cold start buys. Rediscovering it from scratch is not achievable in the budget. LESSON: a KB verdict is attached to a structural property, and 'reference solution exists' is not the property that made cold-seeding win -- 'the reference is MAXIMAL' was.

evidence: NangateOpenCellLibrary.tech.lef: M1 H, M2 V, M3 H, ... M10 V; platform MIN_ROUTING_LAYER=metal2. ariane136 global route: per-layer resource/demand M2 2783086/556703 V, M3 4023240/696874 H, M4 2834351/367795 V, M5 3647228/448846 H, M6 3642237/103321 V, M7 1179990/12013 H, M8 1381604/2474 V.
mechanism: F2 found empirically that the Tier-1 proxy gives vertical routing 1.08-1.87x more capacity than horizontal on every circuit, making the top-5% congestion cells almost entirely horizontal. That looked like an arbitrary benchmark constant. It is not. NanGate45 alternates routing direction by layer starting HORIZONTAL at metal1, and metal1 is reserved for standard-cell internal routing (MIN_ROUTING_LAYER = metal2) -- so signals get FIVE usable vertical layers (M2,4,6,8,10) but only FOUR horizontal (M3,5,7,9). OpenROAD's own global router confirms it on our routed ariane136: vertical resource 10,641,278 vs horizontal 8,850,458 (ratio 1.202, same direction as the proxy's 1.622 though the proxy overstates it), and horizontal runs hotter in practice -- 13.08% utilisation versus 9.68%, an H/V demand ratio of 1.124. So the asymmetry we exploited is a property of the metal stack, not of the benchmark, and should transfer to any technology whose lowest metal is horizontal and reserved.

evidence: 3 DEV circuits (ibm01/ibm09/ibm17), paired A/B at 400s/circuit x 3 seeds: frozen 0.89463/0.88864/0.89280 (mean 0.89202) vs dedicated soft-macro stage 0.89609/0.88965/0.89441 (mean 0.89338); paired delta +0.00136 on all 3 seeds, t=+7.70. Term split of the loss: density -0.00192 (the term whose top-k gradient support the micro stage repairs) paid for by congestion +0.00305. Discrete stage restricted to hard macros +0.08131; to soft macros +0.01029. Top-k gradient support: 68-85% of soft macros receive EXACTLY ZERO density gradient at the converged placement (44-58% at the initial one); 3x widening cuts that to 23-36% and is still worth only ~-0.002. Two identical baselines 40 min apart on the same box differ by 0.0116, which is what made a single-seed -0.0118 look like a result.
mechanism: A mixed problem (246-760 hard macros under a zero-overlap gate, 894-1844 soft macros with NO constraint at all) invites splitting the optimizer by population: give the unconstrained majority a bigger-step continuous optimizer and stop spending gated batch slots on it. Both halves of that reasoning are refuted by measurement. (1) The soft macros are not under-optimized, they are where ALL the gain already is: reverting them to their initial positions costs +0.29/+0.35/+0.58 while reverting the hard macros costs only +0.10/+0.22/+0.13, and applying the optimized HARD placement alone to the untouched soft placement is worth -0.009 to +0.008, i.e. exactly nothing. Hard-macro value is purely CO-ADAPTIVE. (2) A soft-only Adam on the same differentiable relaxation, run from the converged 400s placement, gives EXACTLY 0.00000 improvement in 15/15 cells (5 learning rates spanning 40x x 3 circuits, 1400-4500 steps each) -- and so does the joint all-macro version, 3/3. It is not a bug: the same optimizer started from the initial placement improves by -0.152/-0.192/-0.438 in 30s. The cause is that the relaxation and the exact objective have DIVERGED by then: the surrogate loss falls monotonically while the exact proxy rises by +0.055 to +0.101 within 50 steps. The discrete stage moves the placement into a region the relaxation is wrong about, because it exploits precisely the pin-to-gcell quantization the relaxation dequantizes to obtain a gradient. (3) Restricting the discrete stage to the CONSTRAINED population costs +0.081 (79% of it congestion); soft macros supply 74-84% of all accepted moves. GENERALIZATION: when a surrogate-proposing stage and an exact-gated discrete stage are composed, the surrogate is exhausted for EVERY variable at the moment its own stage converges, so re-pointing it at any subset buys nothing. Split the optimizer by which stage can still make progress, never by which variables are constrained.

evidence: ariane136 ladder, 6 placements differing only in search effort through one identical ORFS flow: TNS = 0 for all six and WNS spans 0.0728-0.1933 ns, i.e. 0.12 ns of spread among OUR OWN placements. Spearman(proxy, WNS) = -0.200, p = 0.70. The original verdict's own evidence line records TNS = 0 in all three of its runs, which is the condition that makes WNS uninformative.
mechanism: A design that meets timing everywhere has no critical path to improve, so worst negative slack reports whichever non-critical path happens to be worst and is not a placement-quality signal. The original verdict read a 0.05-0.12 ns WNS difference as a quality effect; the ladder shows that difference is inside the spread of re-running the same method. Retest at a clock tight enough that TNS becomes non-zero before claiming any timing effect.
